A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ART research, with readable and matchable text, equations, figures, and tables. All 16 pages of v1 and 11 pages of v2 were inspected. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original retinal and planar alignment experiments in Tables 2–4, qualitative comparisons, and sampling and initialization ablations in Figure 8.

after.justification: v2 retains original alignment experiments and adds indoor/outdoor 3D scene results, runtime measurements, and empirical observations about alternative transform representations.

M1.justification: The multiscale architecture, CAL updater, multiplicative/additive fields, and training losses are retained. A limited inference change is reported: v1 describes random correspondence-point selection, including in Figure 5, whereas v2 specifies SIFT-based point selection for testing while retaining random training sampling (Section 4.2).

E1.justification: v2 adds MegaDepth-1500 outdoor and ScanNet-1500 indoor two-view 3D evaluations, substantially extending coverage beyond the retained retinal and planar benchmarks. Oxford-Paris images are also newly reported for pretraining. AnonMC becomes KBSMC with the same collection dates, pair count, split, and results; this is a dataset identification change.

E2.justification: The HPatches comparison in Table 3 retains LoFTR but removes SuperPoint, R2D2, NCNet, SuperGlue, ASPanFormer, and GeoFormer, while adding LightGlue, MatchFormer, and RoMa. This substantially revises the comparator set for an existing benchmark. The retinal and low-resolution comparator sets in Tables 2 and 4 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces pose-error AUC evaluation at 5, 10, and 20 degrees for the new 3D tasks. Its HR training description adds Oxford-Paris pretraining followed by self-supervised fine-tuning, replacing v1's description of training directly on HPatches. Testing also changes from random to detector-selected points. These are reported protocol revisions; they do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The sampling, initialization, and CAL ablation questions are retained and extended to the new 3D datasets, with revised HR curves in Figure 8. Section 4.5 adds runtime comparisons and brief qualitative findings that additive-only prediction performs worse and full affine/projective prediction often fails to converge. The representation analysis lacks a quantified ablation table or detailed protocol.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. Figure 8 presents unbanded performance curves in both versions.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds ART mAUC results of 74.9 on MegaDepth-1500 and 51.1 on ScanNet-1500, versus RoMa's 75.2 and 52.0. HPatches mAUC changes from 78.5 to 78.6 for ART and 69.8 to 75.4 for LoFTR, but identical settings are not established. Per-threshold HPatches results are removed, HR sampling curves change, and runtime results are added: ART 0.16 s and 261 MB, versus LoFTR 1.101 s and GeoFormer 1.150 s. Tables 2 and 4 retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: The added coordinate-wise equations in v2 expand the elementwise transformation already defined in v1. The update equations, initialization, and losses remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs; the added standard pose-error metric does not introduce new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central autoregressive alignment and adjustable-iteration contributions remain. The abstract refines v1's broad outperformance statement into superiority on planar images and comparable performance on 3D scenes. The conclusion also drops its explicit restriction to planar alignment.

C2.justification: v2 explains the gap to RoMa through limited overlap, repetitive structures, and severe degradations that training augmentation cannot fully simulate. It also argues that multiplicative parameters stabilize optimization by reducing translation variance and attributes full affine/projective non-convergence to complexity. The existing fixed-resolution limitation remains.

D1.justification: v2 specifies differentiable RANSAC, identifies the private dataset's institution and ethics approval, and adds measured runtime and memory use. Conversely, it removes the ResNet backbone identification, 128-channel specification, learning-rate halving schedule, precise augmentation details, and most train/test counts formerly in Table 1. These omissions reduce documentation without establishing corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for RoMa, DIFT, differentiable RANSAC, MatchFormer, the new 3D datasets, and Oxford-Paris training data. It removes CrossHomo, the ResNet reference, and several homography-related references. The feature-based, intensity-based, and iterative-refinement organization and ART's main research positioning remain.

P1.justification: v2 tightens prose, consistently uses transform-field terminology, and expands the explanation of pointwise transformations. Image Warping precedes Training ART, and stochastic supervision is redistributed into those discussions rather than removed. Acknowledgements are added, while the overall five-section narrative remains.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted from one column to two, with figures and tables resized and relocated. Table 1 loses its split column, and Table 3 replaces threshold columns with dataset columns. Figure 6 replaces the HPatches–GeoFormer examples with correspondence displays across three datasets; Figure 8 adds curves and changes the HR axis scale and legends.

improvement.justification: The new 3D evaluations and explicit acknowledgement of performance below RoMa make ART's applicability and performance claims better supported and more precise. Runtime measurements and representation explanations also strengthen previously limited support for efficiency and design choices. These gains are moderated by lost architecture, training, and split details and the unquantified representation analysis, yielding a limited overall improvement.
